text: Gradient descent takes each step in the direction of steepest descent.
Here the loss is a narrow valley. It curves ten times more steeply across the valley than along it.
So the steepest direction points mostly across the valley, not along it. Each step overshoots the floor of the valley, and the next step comes back.

With a step size of zero point one eight, each step multiplies the position across the valley by minus zero point eight. That is the zig-zag. Along the valley, each step multiplies the position by zero point eight two, so progress toward the minimum is slow.
The step size is limited by the steepest direction, and the shallow direction pays for it. Rescaling the problem removes the zig-zag, and momentum reduces it.
